subject: Emotions
title: Disgust and the Immune System
description: A quick win: understand Disgust and the Immune System.

hook.text: Seeing someone sneeze on a screen boosts your actual immune response. Your body prepares for attack.

buildup.text: This is the 'behavioral immune system'—a set of disgust reactions that prevent infection before it starts.

discovery.text: Mark Schaller showed that viewing disease cues activates white blood cell production. Disgust is medicine.

twist.text: The system over-fires. It tags unfamiliar people as potential disease threats—fueling xenophobia.

climax.text: During pandemics, disgust toward outsiders spikes. The immune system hijacks social judgment.

punchline.text: Your body's defense system doesn't wait for proof.
